study: Assessment principles and practices - Quality assessments in a digital age
finding: IB's statement of assessment principles: criterion-related, standards carried across sessions, e-marking, moderation; editions 2018, July 2019 (updated Nov 2021), May 2026
note: Primary IB policy document; full text not opened

study: Diploma Programme assessment: principles and practice
finding: Earlier IB policy text; criterion-related not norm-referenced
note: Cited via IB-derived school page; original PDF not found

study: Assessment guide for chief and principal examiners
finding: Grade standard from previous sessions must be carried forward; chief examiner responsible for maintaining standards year to year; seeding for e-marked components; coursework boundaries fixed at course start

study: IB student assessment (web page)
finding: Boundaries agreed by senior examiners and IB staff using judgement, statistical evidence, grade descriptors and teacher feedback; examiners are subject experts

study: Statistical grade boundary setting approaches (SRB research study)
finding: Statistically Recommended Boundaries maintain standards year to year; 'weak criterion referencing'; method sound but assumptions met in only ~half of contexts; weaker than prior-attainment comparable outcomes
note: Independent methodological review; lit review Dec 2021, simulation Sept 2022, exec summary Oct 2022

study: Rasch analysis of IB subject difficulty (Frontiers in Education)
finding: Rasch Partial Credit Model applied to historical IB data to estimate relative subject difficulty; post hoc modelling has limits

study: May 2023 examination session update
finding: IB set distribution of awarded grades back to May 2019 levels after pandemic inflation

study: DP statistical bulletins May 2019-2025
note: Provisional vs final figures differ slightly

study: PYP and MYP student performance on the International Schools' Assessment
finding: IB contracted ACER in 2009 to analyse ISA data; compares PYP/MYP vs non-IB students on ACER's PISA-based ISA
note: Shows IB-ACER relationship is research contracting, not DP assessment design

study: IB graduates in Australian universities: entry and outcomes
finding: After controls IB and non-IB students perform similarly; correlation between secondary grades and university performance higher for IB graduates; IB graduates more likely to complete in 5 years

study: International Baccalaureate students studying at UK HEIs: how do they perform in comparison with A level students?
finding: IB students outperformed in class of degree in most subject areas; continuation 94.7% vs 94.2% (n.s.)

study: UK postsecondary outcomes
finding: IB students more likely to attend top-20 HEI, graduate with honours, pursue further study

study: UK higher education outcomes
authors_or_publisher: Duxbury et al. (HESA) for the IB
finding: Controlling for ability, IB holders 3.02x more likely to get a first and 40% more likely to get 2:1 or above than A level holders

study: Assessing the equivalencies of the UCAS tariff for different qualifications
finding: UCAS tariff overvalued the IB (and BTEC) relative to later university performance

study: UCAS Expert Group report: IB Diploma and the Tariff
finding: Original comparability study admitting IB to the UCAS tariff

study: IB exam score as predictor of college GPA (Florida)
finding: 4,845 Florida students; average IB exam score strongest predictor of college GPA; no comparison group

study: IB diploma recipients vs non-recipients at University of California
finding: Diploma recipients outperformed IB non-recipients; IB exam scores best predictor of college GPA

study: DP alignment with Norwegian upper secondary education
finding: DP and Norwegian Vitnemal compared on objectives, pedagogy and outcomes; Norwegian IB schools 'well equipped' to deliver DP compatibly with Norwegian system

study: DP country alignment studies (Victoria, Ontario, Finland, Singapore, South Korea, US)
finding: Standards alignment of DP courses vs national upper secondary courses

study: Comparative analysis of DP and GCSE mathematics assessment and grades
finding: Grade comparison DP vs GCSE mathematics

study: IB notional ATAR 2021 / fine-grained IB Admissions Score
finding: Whole-score conversion (45->99.95, 44->99.75, 43->99.45) criticised as too generous; replaced by fine-grained conversion using subject percentage marks (results 2023, admission 2024); 60% unchanged, 25% up, 15% down
note: Method precedent: more resolution, not compression

study: UHR decision on IB meritvarde
finding: Maximum meritvarde 20.00 moved from 40-45 IB points to 44-45; later motions report fall in IB applications; 2022 UHR assessment admits 'felaktig meritvardering'
note: Precedent for consequences of stricter conversion

study: Folketing submission on IB conversion (IB 6 = 10.8)
finding: IB conversion to 7-step scale said to disadvantage IB applicants in kvote 1; Danes Worldwide secured annual review (2023)

study: Ny omregningstabell for IB (hoyring)
finding: Table derived statistically (Norsk Regnesentral method) from IB and Norwegian grade distributions; HK-dir: 2.8% of IB applicants vs 0.08% of Norwegian applicants at 6.0; proposal starts at 20 IB points, Norway-only data, from 2030-31; deadline 10.12.2026

study: Pandemic cohorts and completion in Norwegian upper secondary
finding: Weak students completed more easily during pandemic; average grades rose; questions whether cohorts were study-prepared

study: Exam and standpunkt grades: two sides of the same coin?
finding: Relationship between exam and standpunkt grades in Norway

study: KD-commissioned project on quality, grade inflation and segregation (public/private VGS)
finding: New research project on grade inflation in upper secondary schools
